title: What If You Couldn't Feel Where Your Body Was? One Man Can't

scenes.text: What if you lost the sense that tells you where your body is? One man did.
In 1971 a 19-year-old in England caught a virus. His immune system destroyed the sensory nerves below his neck.
He wasn't paralyzed. His muscles worked. But he couldn't feel his limbs, so he couldn't sit up, stand or feed himself.
Doctors expected a wheelchair for life. After a year, he stood, by staring at his body and planning every move.
He walks today. But each step is a decision, and he has to keep watching his limbs.
Take away his sight, with a blindfold or sudden darkness, and he no longer knows where his body is. He would fall.

description:
What if you lost proprioception, the sense that tells you where your body is without looking?
In 1971 a 19-year-old Englishman, known in the medical literature as IW, had a rare autoimmune reaction to an infection that destroyed the sensory nerves from his neck down. He lost touch and all sense of limb position, while his muscles and motor nerves were unharmed, so he was not paralyzed but could not sit up, walk or feed himself. Expected to spend his life in a wheelchair, he taught himself to move again by watching his limbs and planning each movement, and stood unaided after about a year. Decades later every movement is still deliberate, and without vision he cannot control his body; researchers do not simply blindfold him because he would be at risk of falling. His neurologist's book about him is called Pride and a Daily Marathon.
